Bihar’s JEEViKA, the Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society (BRLPS), has completed 20 years, strengthening rural livelihoods, women’s financial inclusion and entrepreneurship through self-help groups (SHGs). Key Points Bihar Rural Livelihoods Project (JEEViKA) About: The Government of Bihar, through the Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society (BRLPS), an autonomous body under the Department of Rural Development, implements the Bihar Rural Livelihoods Project (BRLP), popularly known as JEEViKA, to promote the social and economic empowerment of rural poor. The core strategy of the BRLP programme is to build vibrant and bankable women’s community institutions in the form of self help groups (SHGs), who through member savings, internal loaning and regular repayment become self sustaining organizations. Status: JEEViKA has expanded from 6 self-help groups across 6 blocks to a statewide community network . Network Coverage : 1.81 crore households linked to 13.06 lakh SHGs. Community Institutions: 77,787 Gram Sangathans and 1,683 Cluster-Level Federations. Bank Credit: ₹76,549 crore accessed through SHGs. 6,771 Bank Sakhis facilitate banking services, financial transactions and financial awareness in rural areas. JEEViKA Didi Ki Rasoi: Promotes women’s participation in food services and institutional catering. Developed at a cost of ₹140.95 crore, the project includes industrial infrastructure and a Common Facility Centre (CFC) aimed at strengthening manufacturing, attracting investment and generating employment opportunities in the state. The inauguration marks a significant step towards developing Bihar’s leather and footwear industry by providing entrepreneurs with modern infrastructure, shared facilities and better opportunities to expand their businesses. bihar_raw_news.title: Colt DCS, RMZ begin construction of 64 MW Mumbai data centre - ET Datacenters
bihar_raw_news.content: Investments & Deals 1 min Read Colt DCS, RMZ begin construction of 64 MW Mumbai data centre Colt Data Centre Services and RMZ have started building their third data centre, Mumbai 3, in Navi Mumbai. This facility will add 64 MW of AI-ready capacity to their campus, increasing its operational capacity to 86 MW. ETDatacenters Published On Oct 16, 2026 at 09:00 AM IST Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Highlights Colt DCS and RMZ commenced construction of Mumbai 3 data centre in Navi Mumbai. The facility will add 64 MW of AI-ready capacity, boosting campus total to 86 MW. The joint venture plans to invest $1.7 billion for 250 MW across India. Mumbai 3 will support hyperscale customers with liquid cooling and renewable energy. Colt Data Centre Services ( Colt DCS ) and Bengaluru-based RMZ have begun constructing their third data centre in Navi Mumbai . The Mumbai 3 facility will deliver 64 MW of AI-ready data centre capacity upon completion, the companies announced on Thursday. This development will increase the Navi Mumbai campus's operational capacity to 86 MW. The campus has the potential to deliver up to 148 MW of capacity at full development, the companies said. Colt DCS and RMZ operate as a joint venture, which announced plans in 2024 to invest $1.7 billion in the Indian data centre market. They aim to develop 250 MW of data centre capacity across Mumbai and Chennai. Construction for Mumbai 3 is now underway following the signing of the facility’s first hyperscale customer, the companies said. Ground preparation for the facility began in December 2025. Pratap Mane, country head, DCS, India, stated that data centre demand is evolving rapidly. Customers require larger deployments, higher rack densities, and infrastructure to support intensive AI workloads. The Mumbai 3 facility incorporates advanced cooling capabilities, including liquid cooling . It also features enhanced power infrastructure to support high-density deployments, Mane added. This design enables customers to scale AI and high-performance computing workloads efficiently while maintaining operational resilience. Deepak Chhabria, president at RMZ Digital Infrastructure , said the campus is designed for hyperscalers and neo-cloud providers. It will enable them to scale seamlessly as their capacity and computing needs evolve. The companies also stated that the facility will operate using 100 per cent renewable energy . It has been designed with a closed-loop cooling system, enabling near-zero wastewater from the cooling process. The project is expected to create more than 700 jobs across construction and operations. Comments What are your thoughts?

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 115 ECI directs 17 States & UTs to conduct Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls with 1st ...
national_raw_news.content: The Election Commission has directed 17 States and Union Territories to conduct a Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls with 1st January next year as the qualifying date. These states and UTs are Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal. The Commission said in its letter that it had issued instructions on the 29th of September to undertake a special drive for the enrolment of left-out, young and first-time eligible electors. EC also said that the schedule for SSR in States and UTs where the Special Intensive Revision is ongoing or has recently been completed will be announced later. It added that for Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, where SIR has not been started so far, the schedule for roll revision will be announced in due course of time. The Commission further said that the Electoral Registration Officer of the concerned assembly constituency shall be responsible for ensuring that no eligible citizen is left out while no ineligible person gets included or remains in the Electoral Roll. During the Special Summary Revision, the Chief Electoral Officer, District Election Officers, and Electoral Registration Officers will ensure that every eligible person is enrolled as an elector. Our correspondent reports that since the revision is a Summary Revision in nature, there will be no house-to-house visits by Booth Level Officers to electors. In order to ensure maximum participation of the young and first-time voters, all prospective electors eligible on 1st January 2027 and those who become eligible on 1st April 2027, 1st July 2027, and 1st October 2027 can also send their advance applications for enrolment. Help desks will be set up at the district level to facilitate enrolment of electors, especially migrants, the vulnerable, and marginalised.

national_raw_news.title: APEDA facilitates export of 1.755 tonnes of organic Palmyra jaggery powder from Tamil Nadu to Bulgaria. 21 mins ago 14
national_raw_news.content: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated Export of 1.755 MT of Organic Palmyra Jaggery Powder from Tamil Nadu to Bulgaria. The consignment of National Programme for Organic Production and EU-certified organic Palmyra Jaggery Powder was dispatched yesterday from Erode district of Tamil Nadu to Varna, Bulgaria. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said the consignment marks an important step towards introducing India’s traditional Palmyra-based products to international markets and diversifying the country’s organic export basket. It said that the initiative, which covers 137 acres under organic cultivation, seeks to link Tamil Nadu’s traditional Palmyra-based products market internationally, creating new opportunities for farmers engaged in the organic cultivation. The Ministry highlighted that by developing export-ready products from this resource, the initiative is set to expand market opportunities while supporting producers and the wider value chain. The ministry also noted that the consignment will be shipped by sea through Chennai Port. Derived from Palmyra blossom nectar, Palmyra Jaggery Powder is a better alternative to refined sugar as it offers potential nutritional benefits, including vitamins and minerals. The Palmyra-based products including Jaggery Powder are associated with traditional production practices and the use of the Palmyra palm, which has long been part of the agricultural and cultural landscape of Tamil Nadu.

national_raw_news.title: Mizoram CM Lalduhoma launches 4 digital financial management initiatives to enhance transparency & accountability. 60 mins ago 19
national_raw_news.content: Mizoram Chief Minister Lalduhoma has launched four major digital financial management initiatives of the state government implemented under the Finance Department, which aim to strengthen transparency, accountability and efficiency in the management of public finances. Mizoram Integrated Works Accounts System (MIWAS) will streamline works accounts in six departments – Public Works Department (PWD), Public Health Engineering Department (PHE), Power & Electricity Department (P&E), Irrigation & Water Resources Department (IWRD), Environment, Forest & Climate Change Department (EFCC), and Land Resources, Soil & Water Conservation Department (LRS&WC). It will improve the reconciliation of expenditure figures submitted to the Accountant General and ensure proper submission of expenditure vouchers through the Treasury. The e-Budget Module will enable online preparation and submission of budget proposals through IFMIS, reducing manual work, calculation errors and delays in processing. The e-Sanction Module will facilitate the online processing of expenditure sanctions, enabling proposals to be forwarded electronically from Drawing and Disbursing Officers and Heads of Departments to the concerned Administrative Departments and the Finance Department. It will also help prevent expenditure beyond the available budget. Under 100% DBT, payments under State schemes, including Thlai Thar Leina (funds for purchase of cash crops), Bana Kaih (handholding scheme) and Power Subsidy, will be transferred directly to beneficiaries’ bank accounts after the Treasury passes the bills. Payment status will also be trackable through IFMIS. Addressing the gathering, the Chief Minister highlighted the importance of digital financial management in ensuring transparency and efficient utilisation of public funds. He noted that Mizoram received Rs. 350 crore under SASCI Part IX in the previous year and is preparing to secure approximately Rs. 650 crore under SASCI Part IV and Part IX during 2026-27. The initiatives mark another step towards modernizing financial administration and improving public service delivery in Mizoram.
